answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each agent identity to a refundable stake bond: to join, an agent locks a deposit that is slashed if it is caught sock-puppeting or spamming. An attacker then pays a real, linear cost for every fake identity, so flooding the market gets expensive fast, while honest agents earn their bond back plus reputation over time. Trust grows like a grove from verified roots rather than from raw headcount, and at its nadir, when a newcomer has no history at all, the bond, not mere claims, vouches for it.
